Aim and objectives

Aim. To prepare you to describe the anatomy of the brain, cranial nerves and spinal cord and localise lesions for MRCPsych Paper A.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Describe the functions of the four lobes and locate Broca's area (inferior frontal gyrus) and Wernicke's area (superior temporal gyrus).
  2. Recognise lobar lesion syndromes, such as Gerstmann syndrome from a dominant parietal (angular gyrus) lesion.
  3. Name the twelve cranial nerves in order and state the main function of each.
  4. Describe the dorsal columns, spinothalamic and corticospinal tracts, and explain the deficits in Brown-Sequard syndrome.
  5. Localise a lesion in a clinical vignette from the pattern of deficits.
  6. Answer the chapter's 70 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
